Herald letters

ONE point not addressed in the article by Bob Hope (“Why Britain paid Scottish wind farms £1bn to switch off their turbines”, The Herald, September 7) is the impact of constraint payments in the event of independence.

The article states that the National Energy System Operator (NESO) estimates an £8 billion a year debt arising from constraint payments.

Currently that bill is paid by all UK consumers but, after independence, there will be no UK grid, hence the majority of the cost will have to be underwritten by consumers in Scotland as the bulk of wind farms are in Scottish waters.

That implies an annual addition to household bills of around £2,700 which will have a massive impact on the Scottish economy. Ian Moir, Castle Douglas.
